approach: Teach five high-value verb forms as ready-made chunks the learner can say today, with an x-ray of one sentence, then practice choosing the right chunk in short survival exchanges.
coverage: Quiero = I want: Quiero agua, por favor
Tengo = I have: Tengo una pregunta
Puedo = I can, can I: ¿Puedo pasar? = May I come in?
Voy = I am going: Voy al baño
The ending (-o, or -oy in voy) already means "I", so yo is not needed
Each chunk takes a noun (quiero agua) or a verb in its base form (puedo pagar)
a + el contracts to al: voy al baño, never voy a el baño

blocks.purpose: Explains learning verbs as chunks first, so the learner can speak before studying conjugation.

data.title: Five verbs that do most of the work

paragraphs: You do not need grammar to start speaking. Five verb forms, learned as fixed chunks, cover a huge share of what a visitor or a new neighbor needs to say.

Four of them end in -o (quiero, tengo, puedo, necesito) and voy ends in -oy, and that ending already means "I". So quiero alone means "I want". Spanish speakers usually leave out yo (I) unless they want to stress it.

blocks.purpose: Targets the most common slip with voy: writing a el instead of al.

data.question: How do you say "I am going to the bathroom"?

trapReasons.0: It is a word-for-word copy of "to the", which feels logical.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: English keeps "to" and "the" apart, so the first instinct is a + el. Spanish always fuses them.
data.correctReasoning: a (to) + el (the) is always written and said al: Voy al baño. With la nothing changes: Voy a la tienda.
data.recoveryTip: If you see "a el", squeeze it into "al".

data.takeaway: Quiero, tengo, puedo, voy and necesito each mean "I ..." on their own: add a thing (quiero agua) or a base verb (puedo pagar) and you have a sentence.

checks.prompt: You are lost and want someone to help you. Which sentence says what you need?
checks.rationale: Necesito means I need, so Necesito ayuda is I need help; tengo ayuda would mean I have help, and voy and puedo do not fit a noun this way.

checks.prompt: You knock on an office door. What does "¿Puedo pasar?" ask?
checks.rationale: Puedo is I can or can I, and pasar is to come in or go through, so ¿Puedo pasar? asks permission to come in.

checks.prompt: Type the one Spanish word that means "I have".
checks.rationale: Tengo means I have, as in Tengo una pregunta; the -o already says "I".

checks.prompt: Fill the gap with one word: "___ al baño" (I am going to the bathroom).
checks.rationale: Voy means I am going; voy al baño is the standard way to say it.
checks.hint: The chunk for I am going is three letters long.
